name: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development

raw_payload.title: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development
raw_payload.summary: As agentic systems are increasingly deployed to support complex Web tasks, multi-agent architectures offer greater parallelism, specialization, and task coverage. However, increasing the number of agents does not necessarily improve system performance, as communication, synchronization, redundant work, and coordination overhead may offset the benefits of additional agents. This presents a fundamental scaling challenge for agentic Web systems: how can agent populations be organized to balance task performance and coordination costs? To address this challenge, we systematically investigate the relationship between agent population size, per-agent token consumption, and coordination overhead in collaborative agentic systems. Experiments on complex Web-oriented software development tasks reveal a non-linear scaling pattern: per-agent token consumption initially decreases as the agent population grows, but eventually exhibits diminishing returns. Motivated by these findings, we introduce the Surgical Team Model (STM), a structured coordination framework that organizes agents through role specialization, constrained inter-agent communication, and coordinator-mediated task aggregation. Experiments on full-stack Web application development tasks show that STM achieves competitive task completion quality and comparable token consumption relative to representative baselines, while incurring higher execution latency.
